author: lhourquin
body:
## Ajout et enrichissement de la gestion des candidatures à un rôle de projet, avec notification et consultation détaillée.

- **POST `/projects/:projectId/roles/:roleId/apply`**  
  - Contrôleur : `ProjectRolesController` (`@project-roles.controller.ts`)
  - Commande : `ApplyToProjectRoleCommand` et handler associé (`@apply-to-project-role.command.ts`)
    - Valide l’éligibilité de la candidature (unicité, non-candidature à son propre projet, cohérence des features/goals).
    - Crée une entité `ProjectRoleApplication`.
    - Utilise le service de mailing (`MailingServicePort` via `ResendMailingService` dans `@/mailing/infrastructure/resend.mailing.service.ts`) implémenter par @Jyzdcs  pour envoyer un email au propriétaire du projet lors de chaque nouvelle candidature.
  - La logique d’envoi d’email s’appuie sur l’injection du port `MAILING_SERVICE_PORT` et la structure du payload est conforme à l’interface `SendEmailPayload`.

- **GET `/projects/:projectId/applications`**  
  - Contrôleur : `ProjectController` (`@project.controller.ts`)
  - Query : `GetAllProjectApplicationsQuery` et handler associé (`@get-all-project-application.query.ts`)
    - Vérifie que l’appelant est bien le propriétaire du projet.
    - Récupère toutes les entités `ProjectRoleApplication` associées au projet.
    - Pour chaque candidature, enrichit la réponse avec le profil utilisateur (id, name, avatarUrl) via la relation `Profile` de Prisma.

- **Accès et mapping des données**  
  - Repository : `PrismaProjectRoleApplicationRepository` (`@prisma.project-role-application.repository.ts`)
    - Méthode `findAllByProjectId` : inclut la relation `user.profile` dans l’instruction Prisma.
  - Mapper : `PrismaProjectRoleApplicationMapper` (`@prisma.project-role-application.mapper.ts`)
    - Méthode `toDomain` : reconstitue l’entité `ProjectRoleApplication` en ajoutant le champ optionnel `userProfile` (id, name, avatarUrl), conversion explicite de `null` en `undefined` pour l’avatar.

- **Entité métier**  
  - `ProjectRoleApplication` (`@project-role-application.entity.ts`)
    - Ajout du champ optionnel `userProfile` dans le type et le constructeur.
    - Le champ est ignoré lors de la création, mais enrichi lors de la reconstitution depuis la base.

- **Documentation**  
  - Swagger (`@swagger-doc.example.yml`)
    - Documentation complète des endpoints POST `/projects/{projectId}/roles/{roleId}/apply` et GET `/projects/{projectId}/applications`.
    - Schémas de réponse enrichis avec le champ `userProfile` (nullable), exemples de payloads et de réponses, gestion des cas d’erreur.

- **Sécurité**  
  - Les endpoints GET `/projects/:projectId/applications` sont protégés pour n’être accessibles qu’au propriétaire du projet (vérification dans le handler de la query).

Ces modifications couvrent l’ensemble du flux : soumission de candidature, notification du propriétaire, récupération centralisée des candidatures avec profil utilisateur, et documentation associée.

> Generated on 2025-07-15 06:16:44 UTC by unknown

## Issue

**A `NumberFormatException` occurred in `MainActivity` when the application attempted to parse a date string ("Sat Jul 12 08:25:19 GMT+05:30 2025") as an integer using `Integer.parseInt()`.**  
This caused a fatal crash on the main thread, impacting user experience.

## Fix

- Added input validation before parsing to ensure only numeric strings are passed to `Integer.parseInt()`.
- Implemented date parsing using the appropriate date parsing method when the input is a date string.

## Details

- Checked the input string format before attempting to parse it as an integer.
- Used a date parsing utility (such as `SimpleDateFormat`) to handle date strings.
- Ensured that only valid numeric strings are parsed as integers, and date strings are parsed with the correct date parser.
- Updated the relevant logic in `MainActivity` to prevent similar exceptions.

## Impact

- Prevents application crashes due to invalid parsing of date strings as integers.
- Improves application stability and user experience.
- Ensures correct handling of both numeric and date inputs.

## Notes

- Further input validation and error handling could be added to cover additional edge cases.
- Consider refactoring related input parsing logic throughout the application for consistency.
- No changes to the user interface were made in this update.

## Description
<!--
A clear and concise description of the PR.

`develop-patch`, `develop-minor` or `v5/develop`

How to contribute: https://contribute.getkirby.com
-->

If we want to use backend classes for dialogs and drawers (https://github.com/getkirby/kirby/pull/7380), we need an easy way to use them inside the dialog/drawer routes config. 

## Changelog
<!--
Add relevant release notes: Features, Enhancements, Fixes, Deprecated.
Reference issues from the `kirby` repo or ideas from `feedback.getkirby.com`.
Always mention whether your PR introduces breaking changes.
-->

### Enhancements
- Dialog and drawer routes: support passing a `controller` class name or closure hat returns an object with `::load()` and `::submit()` methods that will be used then as `load`/`submit` event actions. Ideally used with returning a `Kirby\Panel\Controller\Dialog`/`Kirby\Panel\Controller\Drawer` object. If the named class also defines a static `::for()` method, it will be used to create an instance of the class.

## Docs
<!--
Add any notes that help to document the feature/changes. Doesn't need
to be your best writing, just a few words and/or code snippets.
-->

Instead of a `load` and `submit` callback, you can also define a class of  `Kirby\Panel\Controller\Dialog`/`Kirby\Panel\Controller\Drawer` as `controller` for the route:

```php
[
	'pattern' => 'my/drawer',
	'controller' => fn () => new MyDrawer()
],
[
	'pattern'    => ''another/drawer',
	'controller' => MyDrawer::class
]
```



### For review team
<!--
We will take care of the following before merging the PR.
-->

- [x] Add changes & docs to release notes draft in Notion

author: z3moon
body:
This commit refactors the ShaderCompilerService to move the logic for retrieving compiled programs from the cache off the main thread and into the compiler thread pool.

Previously, the cache lookup was performed on the main thread before a compilation job was created. If the cache was slow or contained a large number of entries, this could cause a noticeable stall, impacting application responsiveness.

By moving the cache retrieval into the compilation task, the lookup now happens on the background thread. This alleviates the main thread stall.

BUGS=[430628799]

body:
## Overview

This PR implements support for the **Briscola 500** variant, which is played with 5 cards per player instead of the traditional 3 cards. The implementation maintains full backward compatibility while adding new functionality.

## Changes Made

### 1. Game Variant Configuration
- Added `gameVariants` constants in `Constants.js` for "traditional" and "briscola500"
- Added `VARIANT_CONFIG` mapping to specify cards per hand for each variant

### 2. Enhanced Game Constructor
- Modified `Game` constructor to accept optional `gameVariant` parameter
- Defaults to traditional 3-card variant for backward compatibility

### 3. Dynamic Card Dealing
- Updated `Game.init()` to deal correct number of cards based on selected variant
- Traditional variant: 3 cards per player
- Briscola 500 variant: 5 cards per player

### 4. Variant-Aware Hand Limits
- Enhanced `Hand` class to enforce maximum card limits based on game variant
- Traditional: max 3 cards
- Briscola 500: max 5 cards
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing Hand constructor calls

### 5. Bug Fixes
- Fixed missing `.js` extension in `MiddlePile.js` import
- Resolved middle pile state issue in `_playRound()` method that affected card dealing

## Usage Examples

```javascript
// Traditional variant (default - existing code unchanged)
const game1 = new Game();
game1.init(); // Deals 3 cards per player

// Traditional variant (explicit)
const game2 = new Game({ gameVariant: Constants.gameVariants.TRADITIONAL });
game2.init(); // Deals 3 cards per player

// Briscola 500 variant (new)
const game3 = new Game({ gameVariant: Constants.gameVariants.BRISCOLA_500 });
game3.init(); // Deals 5 cards per player
```

## Backward Compatibility

✅ **All existing code continues to work unchanged**
- Default constructor behavior preserved
- Existing game logic unmodified
- Hand class maintains original constructor signature support

## Testing

All acceptance criteria verified:
- ✅ Game initialization with both variants
- ✅ Correct hand size limits enforced
- ✅ Proper initial card dealing
- ✅ All game mechanics work with both variants
- ✅ Full backward compatibility maintained

The implementation is minimal and surgical, changing only what's necessary to support the new variant while preserving all existing functionality.

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> # Add Support for Briscola 500 Variant
> 
> The current Briscola implementation supports the traditional 3-card variant. This pull request adds support for the "Briscola 500" variant which is played with 5 cards per player instead of 3.
> 
> ## Changes Required
> 
> 1. **Add game variant configuration** - Create a way to specify which variant to play (traditional 3-card or Briscola 500 with 5 cards)
> 
> 2. **Update Constants** - Modify the game constants to support variable hand sizes based on the selected variant
> 
> 3. **Update Game initialization** - Modify the `Game.init()` method to deal the appropriate number of cards based on the selected variant
> 
> 4. **Update Hand class** - Ensure the Hand class can handle up to 5 cards when playing Briscola 500
> 
> 5. **Update game logic** - Ensure all game mechanics work correctly with both 3-card and 5-card variants
> 
> ## Implementation Details
> 
> - Add a `gameVariant` parameter to the Game constructor that defaults to the traditional 3-card variant
> - Create constants for both variants (3-card traditional and 5-card Briscola 500)
> - Update the maximum hand size based on the selected variant
> - Ensure backward compatibility - existing code should continue to work with the traditional 3-card variant
> - Update the initial card dealing logic to deal the correct number of cards based on variant
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> 
> - [x] Game can be initialized with either traditional (3 cards) or Briscola 500 (5 cards) variant
> - [x] Hand size limits are correctly enforced based on the selected variant
> - [x] Initial card dealing works correctly for both variants
> - [x] All existing game logic continues to work with both variants
> - [x] Backward compatibility is maintained - existing code using the default constructor should work unchanged

author: hantangsun
body:
Closes RV-712

Closes RV-718

# What

This MR removes the use of f64 in both interpreted and jit mode of the RISC-V pvm

# Why

Currently the the riscv-pvm uses Floating point types, including rust f64 and Cranelift F64. This is unsafe because:

- Signalling NaNs may actually crash the process the PVM runs in

- Floats may be normalised, causing indeterministic behaviour

Therefore, all floating point type usage needs to be removed 

# How

This MR replaces all f64 usage with u64. The u64 stores the bit value of the `rustc_apfloat` representation of the f64.

For the external functions reading/writing f64 values, `FValue`(which contains the u64) is passed across extern "C" boundaries.

The stored floating point value can be accessed by first casting to u128 and then calling `Double::from_u128_r(input, round)`

# Manually Testing

```
make -C src/riscv all
```

There are currently no tests that checks for floating point usage.

body:
Implementação de funcionalidades:

- Visualizar evento

- Gerenciar inscrição

- Visualizar meus eventos

This pull request introduces significant changes to the backend of the `byPodiumProject` application, focusing on the configuration, models, migrations, and admin interface. These changes aim to establish foundational components for managing event-related data and improve API documentation and middleware support.

### Backend Configuration Updates:
* Added new local apps (`evento`, `usuarios`, `inscricoes`, `localidades`) and third-party apps (`rest_framework`, `drf_yasg`, `corsheaders`) to the `INSTALLED_APPS` section in `settings.py`. Enabled `CorsMiddleware` for handling cross-origin requests.
* Defined `MEDIA_URL` and `MEDIA_ROOT` for managing media files. Added `CORS_ORIGIN_WHITELIST` and `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` to support secure cross-origin requests.

### URL and API Documentation Enhancements:
* Updated `urls.py` to include routes for the `evento` app's API, and added Swagger and ReDoc endpoints for API documentation using `drf_yasg`.

### Admin Interface Improvements:
* Registered models (`evento`, `localidade`, `participante`, `organizador`, `inscricao`, `categoria`, `kit`, `item`, `pagamento`) with custom admin classes to enhance the admin interface. Admin classes include tailored `list_display` attributes for better data visualization.

### Model and Migration Changes:
* Created initial models (`evento`, `participante`, `organizador`, `localidade`, etc.) and migrations to define the schema for event management. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1d10726bb469471eec240cbb13ab8d161765702304826975b853e060fbd68569R1-R68) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c506b02d4f9a878fc97c2bb286174e35af781aed93e6117abf77bbdd2a9d6b13R1-R21) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4b5390523c927165db332fdccd7e25e4d17972d465f325f96df3a223afaa1dd2R1-R66)
* Refactored models by removing redundant fields (`endereco`, `cidade`, `uf`) and replacing them with relationships to the `localidade` model. Simplified and optimized fields in `evento` and `organizador`.
* Removed unused models (`categoria`, `kit`, `item`) and related fields from `inscricao` to streamline the database schema.

### Management Command Addition:
* Added a custom management command (`importa_localidades.py`) to import locality data from a CSV file into the `localidade` model.

body:
## Summary
- Fixed the 'Invalid response from server' error when searching dictionary terms
- Enabled AI generation for missing terms
- Updated frontend validation to accept dictionary backend response format
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing API response formats

## Problems Fixed

### 1. AI Generation Not Triggering
- Added `generateIfMissing: true` parameter when fetching individual terms
- Automatically attempt term generation when search returns no results

### 2. Response Format Mismatch
The dictionary backend returns responses with `success: true/false` field, but the frontend validation was expecting `status: 'success' < /dev/null | 'error'` field. This mismatch caused all valid API responses to be rejected, even when the backend successfully returned AI-generated results.

## Solution
1. Updated `isValidApiResponse` in `dictionarySecurity.ts` to accept both response formats
2. Modified all dictionary API client methods to properly extract data from the nested response structure
3. Added automatic AI generation for missing terms
4. Ensured backward compatibility so existing code continues to work

## Testing
- All unit tests passing (378 tests)
- Pre-commit checks passed
- Validated the fix handles both response formats correctly
- Tested AI generation triggers properly for missing terms

Fixes the issue reported in the screenshots where valid AI-generated dictionary responses were showing as errors.

body:
This PR refactors the `NFLPlayersController` class to eliminate code duplication while maintaining identical functionality. The refactoring extracts common patterns into reusable private helper methods, improving code maintainability and readability.

## Changes Made

### 1. Extracted Data Loading Method
**Before:** JSON file loading code was duplicated in `get_all_players()` and `get_player_by_id()`
```python
# Duplicated in both methods:
base_dir = os.path.dirname(__file__)
json_path = os.path.join(base_dir, "../../data/nfl/nfl_data.json")
with open(json_path) as f:
    nfl_data = json.load(f)
```

**After:** Extracted into `_load_nfl_data()` helper method
```python
def _load_nfl_data(self):
    """Load NFL data from JSON file."""
    base_dir = os.path.dirname(__file__)
    json_path = os.path.join(base_dir, "../../data/nfl/nfl_data.json")
    with open(json_path) as f:
        return json.load(f)
```

### 2. Extracted Collection Retrieval Method
**Before:** ChromaDB collection retrieval was duplicated in similarity methods
```python
# Duplicated in multiple methods:
collection = self.db_client.get_or_create_collection("nfl_players")
```

**After:** Extracted into `_get_collection()` helper method

### 3. Extracted Similarity Calculation Method
**Before:** Similarity calculation logic was duplicated
```python
# Duplicated in multiple places:
similarity = round(1 - distance, 3)
```

**After:** Extracted into `_calculate_similarity_score()` helper method

### 4. Extracted Player Metadata Processing Method
**Before:** Complex player object creation with similarity data was duplicated in `get_similar_players()`

**After:** Extracted into `_process_player_metadata_with_similarity()` helper method

## Benefits Achieved

- **Reduced Code Duplication**: Eliminated ~40 lines of duplicated code
- **Improved Maintainability**: Changes to common patterns only need to be made in one place
- **Enhanced Readability**: Main methods are more focused and easier to understand
- **Better Testability**: Helper methods can be tested independently
- **Preserved Functionality**: All existing endpoints maintain identical behavior

## Public API Unchanged

All public methods maintain their original signatures and behavior:
- `get_all_players()`
- `get_player_by_id(player_id)`
- `get_similar_players(search, top_n=5)`
- `create_vector_space_visualization(player_id)`

## Additional Improvements

- Updated `.gitignore` to exclude Python cache files
- Added comprehensive documentation to helper methods
- Maintained code style consistency throughout

Fixes #2.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a comprehensive graphics system for the Scarlet kernel, addressing the need for graphics functionality with VirtIO GPU support and proper framebuffer abstraction.

## Features Implemented

### VirtIO GPU Device Support
- Added VirtIO GPU device type (16) recognition in the device detection system
- Implemented complete VirtIO GPU driver following existing VirtIO block device patterns
- Added GPU device initialization, feature negotiation, and queue management

### Graphics Device Abstraction
- Created `GraphicsDevice` trait with comprehensive framebuffer operations
- Implemented pixel format support: RGBA8888, BGRA8888, RGB888, RGB565
- Added framebuffer configuration management with width, height, format, and stride
- Provided memory allocation and address mapping for framebuffer operations

### Device Integration
- Extended device manager with `Graphics` device type
- Added `as_graphics_device()` method to the Device trait
- Implemented seamless integration with existing device registration system
- Added utility function `get_graphics_device()` for easy device access

### Architecture Highlights
- Follows existing VirtIO device patterns for consistency
- Maintains architectural harmony with BlockDevice implementation
- Uses existing device manager infrastructure
- Provides extensible foundation for future graphics functionality
- Maintains `no_std` compatibility with proper test annotations

## Files Added/Modified

```
kernel/src/device/graphics/mod.rs         - Graphics device abstraction (new)
kernel/src/drivers/graphics/virtio_gpu.rs - VirtIO GPU driver implementation (new)
kernel/src/drivers/graphics/mod.rs        - Graphics drivers module (new)
kernel/src/device/mod.rs                  - Added Graphics device type
kernel/src/drivers/mod.rs                 - Added graphics module
kernel/src/drivers/virtio/device/mod.rs   - Added GPU device type support
```

## Testing
- Added 7 comprehensive test cases covering all graphics functionality
- All 229 tests pass with 100% success rate
- Tests cover pixel formats, framebuffer configuration, device operations, and utility functions

## Example Usage

```rust
use crate::device::graphics::{get_graphics_device, PixelFormat, FramebufferConfig};

// Get the first available graphics device
if let Some(device) = get_graphics_device() {
    if let Some(graphics) = device.as_graphics_device() {
        // Get framebuffer configuration
        let config = graphics.get_framebuffer_config()?;
        println!("Display: {}x{} {:?}", config.width, config.height, config.format);
        
        // Get framebuffer memory address
        let fb_addr = graphics.get_framebuffer_address()?;
        
        // Flush changes to display
        graphics.flush_framebuffer(0, 0, config.width, config.height)?;
    }
}
```

This implementation provides the foundation for graphics functionality as requested in the original issue, enabling VirtIO GPU framebuffer acquisition with proper abstraction design.

Fixes #155.

     https://github.com/kedacore/keda/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

This PR implements the Force-Activation annotation (as asked for in #6903) which, when set, treats all scalers on a ScaledObject as Active, triggering scale up from 0 if the ScaledObject was previously inactive.

This PR does the following to achieve this goal:
- Add a predicate to the controller to listen for changes on this annotation
- Add a check for the annotation in the scale loop that activates the scaled object if not already activated, sets the Active condition, and adds a message to it
- Add a UT to test the above
- Add an E2E test to test addition and removal of the annotation.

This PR adds a helpful subscript to all GitHub issue templates to encourage users to react with 👍 to help prioritize issues and use comments for providing useful context rather than `+1` or `me too`.

## Changes Made

Added the following subscript to all three issue templates:
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yaml`
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/change_proposal.yaml`
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/new-conventions.yaml`

The subscript appears as a dropdown element with the text:
> <sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).</sub>

## Implementation Details

Since all issue templates are YAML-based issue forms, the subscript was implemented as a dropdown element with:
- A descriptive label "Tip"
- A helpful description explaining its purpose
- A single option containing the subscript text
- `default: 0` to ensure the option is pre-selected

## Testing

- ✅ All YAML files pass syntax validation
- ✅ Code formatting is consistent with repository standards
- ✅ Build system (`make generate-gh-issue-templates`) runs successfully
- ✅ No changes to existing functionality or areas list

Fixes #45.

author: hughhan1
body:
## Description
This commit implements comprehensive support for test class inheritance across modules in `rtest`, addressing the inconsistency with pytest's behavior. Previously, `rtest` only collected test methods defined directly in each test class, ignoring inherited methods from parent classes.

The inheritance resolution works by first collecting all test classes and their relationships during module parsing. When discovering tests, the system recursively resolves base classes through the inheritance chain, collecting test methods from all ancestors. Special handling ensures that classes with `__init__` methods are skipped, along with their entire inheritance chain.

The implementation leverages `ruff_python_semantic`. A new module resolver system handles import resolution and cross-file loading, while a semantic analyzer tracks class relationships and inheritance chains. Additionally, we leverage `ruff_text_size` for source location tracking and `ruff_source_file` for file handling.

This is implemented to address https://github.com/hughhan1/rtest/issues/56.

### Implementation Details
- Enhanced test discovery with semantic analysis using `ruff_python_semantic`
- `ModuleResolver` for handling Python import resolution and module loading
- `SemanticTestDiscovery` for enhanced test discovery with import resolution
- Added cycle detection to prevent infinite recursion in circular inheritance
- Modified visitor pattern to track full inheritance chains with `ResolvedBaseClass`
- Implemented recursive method collection through `get_base_class_methods`
- Added recursive `__init__` checking through entire inheritance chain
- Enhanced `TestClassInfo` to store resolved base class information
- Updated collection nodes to use semantic discovery

### Additional Changes
- Collection warnings for classes with `__init__` constructors
- Warning system with file paths and line numbers
- Graceful handling of unresolvable imports

## Test Plan
Automated tests, including the following that cover the issue highlighted in https://github.com/hughhan1/rtest/issues/56.
```python
def test_parameterized_tests_via_inheritance(self) -> None:
    """
    This addresses the specific case where developers use class inheritance to implement
    parameterized test cases. Both parent and child classes should have their test
    methods collected, allowing the same test logic to run with different parameters.
    
    Example scenario: TestStringConcat and TestStringJoin both run test_concatenation
    but with different operation implementations and expected results.
    """
    files = {
        "test_string_operations.py": textwrap.dedent("""
            class TestStringConcat:
                def test_concatenation(self):
                    result = self.operation(self.input_a, self.input_b)
                    assert result == self.expected
                
                operation = lambda self, a, b: a + b
                input_a = "hello"
                input_b = "world"
                expected = "helloworld"

            class TestStringJoin(TestStringConcat):
                operation = lambda self, a, b: " ".join([a, b])
                expected = "hello world"
        """)
    }

    with create_test_project(files) as project_path:
        result = run_collection(project_path)

        # Should succeed and collect all three parameterized variations
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, f"Parameterized test inheritance should work. Error: {result.stdout + result.stderr}")
        
        output = result.stdout + result.stderr
        
        # Should collect both test methods (one from each class) - fixes the original issue
        # where only the parent class test was collected
        self.assertIn("test_string_operations.py::TestStringConcat::test_concatenation", output)
        self.assertIn("test_string_operations.py::TestStringJoin::test_concatenation", output)
        self.assertIn("collected 2 items", output)

def test_multi_level_parameterized_inheritance(self) -> None:
    """
    This extends the parameterized test case scenario to test inheritance chains where
    each level in the hierarchy represents a different parameterization of the same
    test logic. All classes in the chain should have their test methods collected.
    
    Example: TestBase (identity), TestSquare (x²), TestCube (x³) all run test_operation
    but with progressively different mathematical operations.
    """
    files = {
        "test_multi_param.py": textwrap.dedent("""
            class TestBase:
                def test_operation(self):
                    result = self.operation(self.input_value)
                    assert result == self.expected
                
                operation = lambda self, x: x
                input_value = 5
                expected = 5

            class TestSquare(TestBase):
                operation = lambda self, x: x * x
                expected = 25

            class TestCube(TestSquare):
                operation = lambda self, x: x * x * x
                expected = 125
        """)
    }

    with create_test_project(files) as project_path:
        result = run_collection(project_path)

        # Should succeed and collect all three parameterized variations
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, f"Multi-level parameterized inheritance should work. Error: {result.stdout + result.stderr}")

        output = result.stdout + result.stderr
        
        # Should collect all three test methods (one from each class in the inheritance chain)
        # This ensures no parameterized test variations are missed in deep inheritance hierarchies
        self.assertIn("test_multi_param.py::TestBase::test_operation", output)
        self.assertIn("test_multi_param.py::TestSquare::test_operation", output)
        self.assertIn("test_multi_param.py::TestCube::test_operation", output)
        self.assertIn("collected 3 items", output)
```

- Monitors network quality and alerts the user on degradation.
- Provides game state saving and restoration upon reconnection.
- Caches user operations during disconnection to be replayed on reconnect.
- Offers user-friendly error messages for common WebSocket issues.

author: silverlightning926
body:
Currently, project dependencies and tasks such as running the server through bash files, and items such as virtual environments are managed manually. This can get a bit messy and daunting to newcomers and non-technical contributors.

This is where [PDM](https://pdm-project.org/) or other python build tools can help. After installing Python and [installing PDM](https://pdm-project.org/en/latest/#installation), users will be `pdm sync` to automatically create a virtual environment (`.venv`), activate it, and pull all the dependencies and install them for the project and can even run `pdm sync --group insiders` to get the insider dependencies as well assuming they have access to it. They can also run `pdm run serve` (or `pdm run serve-insiders`) to start up the servers (basically aliasing `mkdocs serve`) along with with different run commands that allow you do start the server in insider mode, build the side, and more. And all of it can be managed either through the command line or through the `pyproject.toml` file at the base of the project. Therefore, it mostly takes care about handling dependencies, commands, and managing the virtual environment, and more.

Wanted to submit this in draft to propose this as a idea and wanted to gauge how yall feel about it before I update the documentation and onboarding stuff and add it to this PR. Let me know if you have any concerns or questions and I will try my best to answer them.

I chose PDM over other options bc its the most full fledged option, with all the tools that would be useful to us while not being too heavy. But there are other options like uv, poetry, or hatch, but they all are either overkill or are missing features that would be useful.

Also the lock file keeps track of all the package versions and makes sure you are getting the right package version by creating a hash of the package. But I cannot currently add the mkdocs material insiders package fork to the lock as I don't have access to it. So if someone who does have access could run `pdm lock` to add it to the lock file and commit it, that would be much appreaciated!

## 코드 변경 이유 - 위치 기반 사용자 인증 기능 구현을 위해 TblUser 엔티티에 사용자의 현재 위치(위도, 경도)를 저장할 필드 필요 - 해당 엔티티에 대한 데이터 접근을 담당할 TblUserRepository 인터페이스를 정의
## 구현 사항 - com.kangwon.fino.domain.TblUser.java 파일에 latitude (Double), longitude (Double) 필드 추가 - com.kangwon.fino.repository.TblUserRepository.java 인터페이스 생성 - JpaRepository을 상속받아 TblUser 엔티티에 대한 기본 CRUD 기능을 제공받도록 함
## 발견 위험/장애 - ERD/DB 정규화 담당 팀원과의 협의 필요
## 테스트 완료 및 계획 - 추후 위치 기반 사용자 인증 기능이 완성되면 테스트 진행할 예정
## To Reviewers - 코드가 적합한지 확인 부탁 **Closes #6**

### Checklist (for reviewing)

#### Functionality

- [ ] **Are all requirements met?** Compare implemented functionality with the requirements specification.
- [ ] **Does the UI work as expected?** There should be no Javascript errors in the console; all resources should load. There should be no unexpected errors. Deliberately try to break the feature to find out if there are corner cases that are not handled.

#### Code

- [ ] **Do you fully understand the introduced changes to the code?** If not ask for clarification, it might uncover ways to solve a problem in a more elegant and efficient way.
- [ ] **Does the PR introduce any inefficient database requests?** Use the debug server to check for duplicate requests.
- [ ] **Are all necessary strings marked for translation?** All strings that are exposed to users via the UI must be [marked for translation](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/1.10/topics/i18n/translation/).

#### Tests

- [ ] **Are there sufficient test cases?** Ensure that all components are tested individually; models, forms, and serializers should be tested in isolation even if a test for a view covers these components.

- [ ] **If this is a new feature or a significant change to an existing feature?** has the manual testing spreadsheet been updated with instructions for manual testing?

- [ ] **Are changes to the API documented in the API docs?** If this PR introduces new API functionality or changes existing ones, the changes must be documented.
- [ ] **Are reusable components documented?** If this PR introduces components that are relevant to other developers (for instance a mixin for a view or a generic form) they should be documented in the Wiki.

author: lalithsrinivas
body:
# PR Details

We were seeing a really big memory overhead when trying to get cell style for each cell separately. This patch adds new public API to the library which lets us get Column values and their corresponding styleIDs per row.

## Description

Made use of the `getValueFrom` method which has access to `styleID` of the cell by creating new method which returns cell's StyleID along with value of the cell. Created new `ColumnsWithCorrespondingStyleIDs` API which uses the updated `getValueAndStyleFrom` method.

author: leotseng-suse
body:
#### Pull Requests Rules

- `Never remove an already released chart!`
  - This does not apply to RC's because they are not released.
- Each Pull Request should only modify one chart with its dependencies.

- Pull request title:

    ```
    [dev-v2.X] <chart> <version> <action>
    ```

  - `<action>`: 1 of (bump; remove; UnRC)

---

##### Checkpoints for Chart Bumps

`release.yaml`:

- [ ] Each chart version in release.yaml DOES NOT modify an already released chart. If so, stop and modify the versions so that it releases a net-new chart.
- [ ] Each chart version in release.yaml IS exactly 1 more patch or minor version than the last released chart version. If not, stop and modify the versions so that it releases a net-new chart.

`Chart.yaml and index.yaml`:

- [ ] The `index.yaml` file has an entry for your new chart version.
- [ ] The `index.yaml` entries for each chart matches the `Chart.yaml` for each chart.
- [ ] Each chart has ALL required annotations
  - kube-version annotation
  - rancher-version annotation
  - permits-os annotation (indicates Windows and/or Linux)

---

Fill the following only if required by your manager.

##### Issue: <!-- link the issue or issues this PR resolves here -->
<!-- If your PR depends on changes from another pr link them here and describe why they are needed in your solution section. -->

##### Solution
<!-- Describe what you changed to fix the issue. Relate your changes back to the original issue / feature and explain how this addresses the issue. -->

author: mpwarres
body:
https://github.com/WAVM/WAVM has not been updated in 3 years and doesn't build with C++20. This change removes WAVM from the proxy-wasm-cpp-host build, to unblock updating build rules to use C++20, which in turn unblocks updating to a recent version of v8, which requires C++20 to build.

WAVM was already removed from the Envoy build in https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/pull/32872.

author: rajendraindukuri
body: # Description In a single or stretched cluster, when a failover occurs, we remap the Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) from the source Persistent Volume (PV) to the replicated PV. However, this process leaves the claimRef field on the source PV empty, allowing any user to potentially claim it. To prevent this, this Pull Request (PR) updates the claimRef field to reserved/reserved in these scenarios, effectively blocking the PV from being claimed by unauthorized users. # GitHub Issues List the GitHub issues impacted by this PR: | GitHub Issue # | | -------------- | | https://github.com/dell/csm/issues/1924 | # Checklist: - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code to ensure there are no formatting, vetting, linting, or security issues - [x] I have verified that new and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes - [x] I have not allowed coverage numbers to degenerate - [ ] I have maintained at least 90% code coverage - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] I have maintained backward compatibility # How Has This Been Tested? Tested the Failover and reprotect workflow on single cluster for PowerFlex and the screenshots are as below: Status of PV, PVC and RG before Failover Status of PV, PVC and RG after Failover (original PV "claimRef" has been updated to reserved/reserved and original PVC is now claiming to replicated PV ) After reprotect on the RG

author: dbolduc
body:
Fixes #1699 

Captures error details from tonic, and surfaces them in our `gax::error::rpc::Status`.

gRPC is weird. They send the code in `grpc-status`, and the message in `grpc-message`, and then they also encode a full `google.rpc.Status` proto (which has a `code` and `message` field) in `grpc-status-details-bin`. Seems redundant to me. I will just assume they are always the same :shrug:. If they aren't the non-binary headers will win.

https://docs.rs/tonic/0.13.1/src/tonic/status.rs.html#442-457

Added an integration test, to confirm the weirdness.

This pull request simplifies the `AuthProvider` component in `src/contexts/AuthProvider.jsx` by removing unused or redundant methods related to token management and session handling. These changes streamline the codebase and reduce complexity.

### Removed unused methods:

* Removed the `logoutAll` method, which was responsible for logging out all sessions. This method is no longer referenced in the codebase.
* Removed the `getUserTokens` method, which fetched user tokens from the API.
* Removed the `revokeToken` method, which revoked a specific token by its ID.
* Removed the `cleanupTokens` method, which cleaned up expired tokens.

### Updated `value` object:

* Removed references to `logoutAll`, `getUserTokens`, `revokeToken`, and `cleanupTokens` from the `value` object provided by the `AuthContext`.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [mypy](https://pypi.org/project/mypy) from **1.16.1** to **1.17.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 1.17
   ```
   We’ve just uploaded mypy 1.17 to the Python Package Index ([PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/mypy/)).
Mypy is a static type checker for Python. This release includes new features and bug fixes.
You can install it as follows:

    python3 -m pip install -U mypy

You can read the full documentation for this release on [Read the Docs](http://mypy.readthedocs.io).

 Optionally Check That Match Is Exhaustive

Mypy can now optionally generate an error if a match statement does not
match exhaustively, without having to use `assert_never(...)`. Enable
this by using `--enable-error-code exhaustive-match`.

Example:

python
 mypy: enable-error-code=exhaustive-match

import enum

class Color(enum.Enum):
    RED = 1
    BLUE = 2

def show_color(val: Color) -> None:
     error: Unhandled case for values of type "Literal[Color.BLUE]"
    match val:
        case Color.RED:
            print("red")


This feature was contributed by Donal Burns (PR [19144](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19144)).

 Further Improvements to Attribute Resolution

This release includes additional improvements to how attribute types
and kinds are resolved. These fix many bugs and overall improve consistency.

* Handle corner case: protocol/class variable/descriptor (Ivan Levkivskyi, PR [19277](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19277))
* Fix a few inconsistencies in protocol/type object interactions (Ivan Levkivskyi, PR [19267](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19267))
* Refactor/unify access to static attributes (Ivan Levkivskyi, PR [19254](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19254))
* Remove inconsistencies in operator handling (Ivan Levkivskyi, PR [19250](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19250))
* Make protocol subtyping more consistent (Ivan Levkivskyi, PR [18943](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/18943))

 Fixes to Nondeterministic Type Checking

Previous mypy versions could infer different types for certain expressions
across different runs (typically depending on which order certain types
were processed, and this order was nondeterministic). This release includes
fixes to several such issues.

* Fix nondeterministic type checking by making join with explicit Protocol and type promotion commute (Shantanu, PR [18402](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/18402))
* Fix nondeterministic type checking caused by nonassociative of None joins (Shantanu, PR [19158](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19158))
* Fix nondeterministic type checking caused by nonassociativity of joins (Shantanu, PR [19147](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19147))
* Fix nondeterministic type checking by making join between `type` and TypeVar commute (Shantanu, PR [19149](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19149))

 Remove Support for Targeting Python 3.8

Mypy now requires `--python-version 3.9` or greater. Support for targeting Python 3.8 is
fully removed now. Since 3.8 is an unsupported version, mypy will default to the oldest
supported version (currently 3.9) if you still try to target 3.8.

This change is necessary because typeshed stopped supporting Python 3.8 after it
reached its End of Life in October 2024.

Contributed by Marc Mueller
(PR [19157](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19157), PR [19162](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19162)).

 Initial Support for Python 3.14

Mypy is now tested on 3.14 and mypyc works with 3.14.0b3 and later.
Binary wheels compiled with mypyc for mypy itself will be available for 3.14
some time after 3.14.0rc1 has been released.

Note that not all features are supported just yet.

Contributed by Marc Mueller (PR [19164](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19164))

 Deprecated Flag: `--force-uppercase-builtins`

Mypy only supports Python 3.9+. The `--force-uppercase-builtins` flag is now
deprecated as unnecessary, and a no-op. It will be removed in a future version.

Contributed by Marc Mueller (PR [19176](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19176))

 Mypyc: Improvements to Generators and Async Functions

This release includes both performance improvements and bug fixes related
to generators and async functions (these share many implementation details).

* Fix exception swallowing in async try/finally blocks with await (Chainfire, PR [19353](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19353))
* Fix AttributeError in async try/finally with mixed return paths (Chainfire, PR [19361](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19361))
* Make generated generator helper method internal (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19268](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19268))
* Free coroutine after await encounters StopIteration (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19231](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19231))
* Use non-tagged integer for generator label (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19218](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19218))
* Merge generator and environment classes in simple cases (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19207](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19207))

 Mypyc: Partial, Unsafe Support for Free Threading

Mypyc has minimal, quite memory-unsafe support for the free threaded
builds of 3.14. It is also only lightly tested. Bug reports and experience
reports are welcome!

Here are some of the major limitations:
* Free threading only works when compiling a single module at a time.
* If there is concurrent access to an object while another thread is mutating the same
  object, it's possible to encounter segfaults and memory corruption.
* There are no efficient native primitives for thread synthronization, though the
  regular `threading` module can be used.
* Some workloads don't scale well to multiple threads for no clear reason.

Related PRs:

* Enable partial, unsafe support for free-threading (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19167](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19167))
* Fix incref/decref on free-threaded builds (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19127](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19127))

 Other Mypyc Fixes and Improvements

* Derive .c file name from full module name if using multi_file (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19278](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19278))
* Support overriding the group name used in output files (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19272](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19272))
* Add note about using non-native class to subclass built-in types (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19236](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19236))
* Make some generated classes implicitly final (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19235](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19235))
* Don't simplify module prefixes if using separate compilation (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR [19206](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19206))

 Stubgen Improvements

* Add import for `types` in `__exit__` method signature (Alexey Makridenko, PR [19120](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19120))
* Add support for including class and property docstrings (Chad Dombrova, PR [17964](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/17964))
* Don't generate `Incomplete | None = None` argument annotation (Sebastian Rittau, PR [19097](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19097))
* Support several more constructs in stubgen's alias printer (Stanislav Terliakov, PR [18888](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/18888))

 Miscellaneous Fixes and Improvements

* Combine the revealed types of multiple iteration steps in a more robust manner (Christoph Tyralla, PR [19324](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19324))
* Improve the handling of "iteration dependent" errors and notes in finally clauses (Christoph Tyralla, PR [19270](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19270))
* Lessen dmypy suggest path limitations for Windows machines (CoolCat467, PR [19337](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19337))
* Fix type ignore comments erroneously marked as unused by dmypy (Charlie Denton, PR [15043](https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/15043))

    monkeypatch.setenv("GIT_USERNAME", "user\nname")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GH_TOKEN", "token\nvalue")
    codeflash_output = scanner._authenticate_by_access_token(); result = codeflash_output # 1.98μs -> 1.76μs (12.4% faster)


def test_username_and_token_with_equals_sign(scanner, monkeypatch):
    """Test username and token containing equals sign (common in tokens)."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("GIT_USERNAME", "user=eq")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GH_TOKEN", "tok=eq")
    codeflash_output = scanner._authenticate_by_access_token(); result = codeflash_output # 2.08μs -> 1.81μs (14.6% faster)


# ----------------------
# Large Scale Test Cases
# ----------------------

def test_large_username_and_token(scanner, monkeypatch):
    """Test with large username and token (999 chars each)."""
    username = "u" * 999
    token = "t" * 999
    monkeypatch.setenv("GIT_USERNAME", username)
    monkeypatch.setenv("GH_TOKEN", token)
    codeflash_output = scanner._authenticate_by_access_token(); result = codeflash_output # 2.77μs -> 2.39μs (16.0% faster)


def test_many_calls_with_different_envs(scanner, monkeypatch):
    """Test calling the function repeatedly with different environment values."""
    for i in range(100):
        uname = f"user{i}"
        tval = f"token{i}"
        monkeypatch.setenv("GIT_USERNAME", uname)
        monkeypatch.setenv("GH_TOKEN", tval)
        codeflash_output = scanner._authenticate_by_access_token(); result = codeflash_output # 106μs -> 96.1μs (10.6% faster)


def test_many_calls_with_missing_envs(scanner, monkeypatch):
    """Test calling the function repeatedly with missing environment variables."""
    # Alternate between missing username and missing token
    for i in range(50):
        if i % 2 == 0:
            monkeypatch.delenv("GIT_USERNAME", raising=False)
            monkeypatch.setenv("GH_TOKEN", f"token{i}")
        else:
            monkeypatch.setenv("GIT_USERNAME", f"user{i}")
            monkeypatch.delenv("GH_TOKEN", raising=False)
        with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
            scanner._authenticate_by_access_token()
# codeflash_output is used to check that the output of the original code is the same as that of the optimized code.

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a comprehensive Supabase authentication system to the mentor app, enabling secure user registration, login, and session management.

## ✨ New Features
- **🔐 Complete Authentication System**: Email/password authentication powered by Supabase
- **📝 User Registration**: Signup screen with password validation and email verification
- **🔑 Secure Login**: Login screen with comprehensive error handling and loading states
- **💾 Session Management**: Persistent authentication state that survives app restarts
- **🛡️ Protected Navigation**: Automatic routing based on user authentication status
- **👤 User Profile Integration**: Display user email and secure logout functionality

## 🛠️ Technical Implementation
- **Supabase Client**: Configured with AsyncStorage for secure session persistence
- **Authentication Context**: React context providing global auth state management
- **Authentication Service**: Comprehensive service layer handling all auth operations
- **React Native Compatibility**: Added polyfills for browser APIs (structuredClone fix)
- **Enhanced Navigation**: Updated app navigator to handle authenticated/unauthenticated flows

## 📦 Dependencies Added
- `@supabase/supabase-js`: Core Supabase client library for authentication
- `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage`: Secure local storage for session data

## 🔧 Files Changed
### New Files:
- `src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx`: Global authentication state management
- `src/services/supabaseClient.ts`: Supabase client configuration
- `src/services/authService.ts`: Authentication service layer
- `src/screens/LoginScreen.tsx`: User login interface
- `src/screens/SignupScreen.tsx`: User registration interface  
- `src/screens/AuthScreen.tsx`: Combined auth flow with login/signup toggle

### Modified Files:
- `src/navigation/AppNavigator.tsx`: Added auth-based navigation logic
- `src/screens/ProfileScreen.tsx`: Integrated user data and logout functionality
- `src/polyfills.ts`: Added structuredClone polyfill for React Native compatibility
- `src/types/env.d.ts`: Added Supabase environment variable types

## 🔒 Security Features
- Password validation (minimum 6 characters)
- Secure session storage with AsyncStorage
- Automatic token refresh
- Environment variable protection for API keys
- Logout confirmation dialog

## 🎯 User Experience
- ⏳ Loading states during authentication operations
- ❗ Error handling with user-friendly messages
- 🔄 Smooth transitions between auth and main app
- 💾 Persistent login state across app restarts
- ✅ Email verification support

## 🧪 Test Plan
- [ ] Test user registration with valid email/password
- [ ] Test user login with existing credentials
- [ ] Verify session persistence after app restart
- [ ] Test logout functionality
- [ ] Verify navigation flows for authenticated/unauthenticated users
- [ ] Test error handling for invalid credentials
- [ ] Verify password validation requirements

## 🔗 Related Issues
Resolves user authentication requirements for the mentor app.

I'm not sure what the optimum order of keyservers should be, but this seems like a good starting point.

This will fix #173

author: onkwon
body:
This pull request refactors the handling of charger events, availability, and configuration in the OCPP module. Key changes include modifying event definitions, improving availability processing logic, and refining checkpoint handling to ensure more precise event dispatching and state updates.

### Refactoring of Event Definitions:
* Updated the values of `ocpp_charger_event_t` enums to use simpler bitwise flags (`0x01`, `0x02`, `0x04`) instead of offsets from a base value for better clarity and maintainability. (`include/charger/ocpp.h`, [include/charger/ocpp.hL49-R51](diffhunk://#diff-d824798fa73531fdb6716ab890988686e98fce084c818c15d465a7cc5807283aL49-R51))

### Improvements to Availability Processing:
* Added logic to handle `CONNECTOR_0` explicitly during availability processing, ensuring proper handling of connector-specific availability changes. (`src/charger/extension_ocpp.c`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-31c6326397de5ad37e271ffdf9ee037369d2c8a317b2a690cb11fcdc00abc90aL130-R132) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-31c6326397de5ad37e271ffdf9ee037369d2c8a317b2a690cb11fcdc00abc90aR141)
* Refined the availability update logic to use `ocpp_charger_get_availability` for determining the state, improving consistency across the codebase. (`src/charger/extension_ocpp.c`, [src/charger/extension_ocpp.cR156-R159](diffhunk://#diff-31c6326397de5ad37e271ffdf9ee037369d2c8a317b2a690cb11fcdc00abc90aR156-R159))

### Refinements in Checkpoint Handling:
* Introduced explicit handling for `CONNECTOR_0` in `do_change_availability` to ensure accurate updates to charger availability and proper event dispatching. (`src/charger/ocpp/handler.c`, [src/charger/ocpp/handler.cL198-R218](diffhunk://#diff-bf5d4fd43f1917f7d019036c8373691abf6286f2aa411bdeadac4a89bb069651L198-R218))

author: mervinpraison
body:
Fixes #918: Ollama sequential tool calling parameter mixing

## Problem
Ollama was generating tool calls with mixed arguments where parameters from different functions were combined, causing functions to receive invalid parameters.

## Solution
- Added parameter validation method `_validate_and_filter_ollama_arguments()`
- Filters invalid parameters before tool execution for Ollama providers
- Prevents functions from receiving unexpected keyword arguments
- Maintains backward compatibility and graceful error handling

## Testing
- Comprehensive test suite validates all scenarios
- All tests pass successfully

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

  * Added new tests to verify argument validation and filtering for Ollama tool calls, as well as provider detection logic.

author: retrotails
body:
so I think this problem was a *lot* simpler than I thought. it looks like when these lines were written originally, the column order was backwards. `[0][2]` and `[1][2]` are both always 0.0 in my testing, unused elements of the matrix as far as I can tell, while `[2][0]` and `[2][1]` appear to be the intended ones.

note that this fixes voxel GI and SDFGI, but *not* screen space effects. thus, this is only a partial fix for https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/108508. these exact same lines also exist in `ss_effects.cpp`, and applying the same fix here *does* fix the X axis, but it does not fix the Y axis, so I'm leaving it as-is for someone else to tackle, because I think at least SSR might need more work than just this projection fixed in order to support an offset frustum.

author: amachino
body:
This pull request introduces several updates to the `Qubex` documentation and examples, focusing on improving clarity, updating parameter values, and removing outdated or redundant code. The changes span multiple Jupyter notebooks and the `README.md` file, with adjustments to experiment configurations, parameter handling, and visualization methods.

### Documentation Updates

* **`README.md`**: Updated the project title from "Quantum Experiment Framework" to "Qubit Experiment Framework" for consistency with the project's scope.

### Notebook Enhancements and Simplifications

#### Analysis Examples (`docs/examples/analysis/fitting.ipynb`):
* Removed redundant code cells, including examples of cosine fitting and double resonator reflection, to streamline the notebook. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8404859b4cfe0f75e8a8d1bb35ec505eafa001dab3d4c01911b505d191d93637L51-L88) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8404859b4cfe0f75e8a8d1bb35ec505eafa001dab3d4c01911b505d191d93637L495-L545)
* Updated parameter values for fitting functions, such as modifying amplitude (`A`), phase (`phi`), and other parameters to reflect more realistic or simplified scenarios. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8404859b4cfe0f75e8a8d1bb35ec505eafa001dab3d4c01911b505d191d93637L251-R216) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8404859b4cfe0f75e8a8d1bb35ec505eafa001dab3d4c01911b505d191d93637L284-R249)
* Simplified visualization calls, e.g., replacing dictionary-based input with direct data input for `scatter_iq_data`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8404859b4cfe0f75e8a8d1bb35ec505eafa001dab3d4c01911b505d191d93637L266-R228) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8404859b4cfe0f75e8a8d1bb35ec505eafa001dab3d4c01911b505d191d93637L301-R263)

#### Backend Examples (`docs/examples/backend/state_manager.ipynb`):
* Removed the entire notebook, including examples of using the `StateManager` class and synchronizing states between Qubex and devices, as it may no longer be relevant or necessary.

#### Basic Usage Examples (`docs/examples/experiment/0_basic_usage.ipynb`):
* Replaced `chip_id="xxQ"` with `chip_id="xxx"` and removed unused parameters like `config_dir` to simplify experiment initialization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-61ba68f99673f88242488864e9df34d6c2c573f14cd46a6e9a3692e597ebc4c4R22-L27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-61ba68f99673f88242488864e9df34d6c2c573f14cd46a6e9a3692e597ebc4c4L128-R117)
* Updated method calls, such as replacing `ex.tool.print_chip_info("chip_summary")` with `ex.tool.print_chip_info()` for clarity.
* Removed sections on Rabi oscillation and related plots, focusing on essential experiment steps.
* Improved comments and descriptions for better readability, e.g., clarifying the purpose of waveforms and measurements. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-61ba68f99673f88242488864e9df34d6c2c573f14cd46a6e9a3692e597ebc4c4L128-R117) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-61ba68f99673f88242488864e9df34d6c2c573f14cd46a6e9a3692e597ebc4c4L155-L157)

#### Spectroscopy Examples (`docs/examples/experiment/1_spectroscopy.ipynb`):
* Added a new cell to demonstrate connecting to instruments before running experiments.
* Enhanced comments to explain the purpose of readout power and amplitude settings during spectroscopy.

These updates collectively enhance the usability and readability of the documentation and examples, making them more accessible to users while removing outdated or redundant content.

DiscussionLinks are displayed in the ActionBar based on if a discussionId is returned from the utils function. We simplified this logic significantly with this PR: https://github.com/republik/plattform/pull/1108/files#diff-86982bc6e1fa863a7dca70981ae6a6a571aeb154130da36b7f93cbc45f110100 but missed that "closed" discussions would return undefined discussionId and thus prevent rendering of the Links.

Tested locally againts the live API

closes #44

- 랭킹 기간(period)에 따라 인기 도서 목록 조회

- N+1 문제 회피: DTO Projection 방식 사용
- 테스트 커버리지 100% 확인 (`DashboardController`, `DashboardServiceImpl`, `CustomRepository`)

### 스크린샷 (선택)

author: mannreis
body:
As faced in during https://github.com/fsspec/kerchunk/pull/565 the tests were failing likely because installing zarr via pip `git+https://github.com/zarr-developers/zarr-python` would provide a unstable version of `zarr` (3.0.9+devXXX). 

I get that would be nice to always test using the zarr `main` branch to catch issues yearly on but I fear this makes it harder to probe for real issues with kerchunk.

So this PR:
- Leaves only the option of using a relased version of zarr installed via `condaforge`.
- It also locks it to `>=3.0.1` as seen in [`pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/fsspec/kerchunk/blob/main/pyproject.toml#L27)
- Enables the option to manually trigger the tests again if there's need be (as currently `zarr-python` main branch is `3.1.0`)

If you do want to run the tests against the latest python, I think cherry-picking  b5038f685796022350bd528c8bb35a71c4e1748 would allow everyone to rerun the tests manually (I think you can already do it @martindurant).

body:
## Problem
The application had scattered styling with hardcoded values across multiple files:
- `static/styles.css` with hardcoded colors and sizes
- Inline styles in HTML files (`demo-modular.html`, `enhanced-architecture-demo.html`)
- Hardcoded styles in JavaScript code
- Duplicated styling between files
- Difficult to maintain consistency and change themes

## Solution
Implemented a comprehensive design system with centralized tokens and theme management:

### 🎯 **Key Features**
- **Design Tokens**: Centralized color, typography, spacing, and shadow definitions
- **CSS Custom Properties**: All hardcoded values replaced with CSS variables
- **Theme Manager**: Dynamic theme switching and runtime customization
- **Component Styles**: Predefined styles for buttons, panels, forms, and tabs
- **Developer API**: Easy-to-use utilities for theme manipulation
- **Backward Compatibility**: Existing functionality preserved with legacy value support

### 📁 **Design System Structure**
```
src/design-system/
├── tokens/
│   ├── colors.js          # Color palette definitions
│   ├── typography.js      # Font and text styles
│   ├── spacing.js         # Spacing and layout values
│   ├── shadows.js         # Shadow and effect definitions
│   └── index.js           # Token exports
├── themes/
│   ├── default.js         # Default theme configuration
│   └── index.js           # Theme management
├── components/
│   └── index.js           # Component style definitions
├── css-generator.js       # CSS custom properties generator
├── theme-manager.js       # Theme management system
├── utils.js               # Utility functions
├── config.js              # Configuration options
└── index.js               # Main entry point
```

### 🚀 **Usage Examples**
```javascript
// Change primary color instantly
designSystemUtils.setColor('primary-500', '#FF5722');

// Update multiple colors at once
designSystemUtils.applyColorSet({
  'primary-500': '#7C3AED',
  'primary-600': '#6D28D9'
});

// Switch entire theme
designSystemUtils.switchTheme('dark');
```

### 📊 **Changes Made**
- **`static/styles.css`**: Replaced 200+ hardcoded values with CSS custom properties
- **`demo-modular.html`**: Updated inline styles to use design system tokens
- **`enhanced-architecture-demo.html`**: Migrated to design system variables
- **`src/main.js`**: Integrated design system initialization
- **Build Process**: Added design system to compilation

### ✅ **Benefits**
- **Centralized**: All styling decisions in one place
- **Consistent**: Unified design language across the application
- **Maintainable**: Change entire color scheme with single file edit
- **Performant**: CSS custom properties are native and fast
- **Scalable**: Easy to add new themes and components
- **Developer-friendly**: Simple API for customization

### 🎨 **Visual Results**

**Main Application with Design System:**
![Main App](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0154cf9-598a-4aac-9e4e-20549d15c98c)

**Demo Page with Consistent Styling:**
![Demo Page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f93509c-5185-466b-b3cb-6c0371a5678a)

**Design System Test Page:**
![Design System Test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdda85a8-6d7d-4f2e-b81c-1296c65bd945)

### 🔧 **Technical Implementation**
- **CSS Custom Properties**: All styles now use `var(--token-name)` format
- **Token System**: Hierarchical design tokens with semantic naming
- **Theme Management**: Runtime theme switching with event system
- **Legacy Support**: Maintains compatibility with existing code
- **Performance**: No JavaScript overhead for basic styling

The design system successfully addresses all styling inconsistencies while providing a foundation for future design improvements and easy theme customization.

author: blaack007
body:
This commit introduces a complete category subscription system, allowing users to subscribe to topics of interest and receive email confirmations.

Key features include:
- A `Subscription` model to track user-category relationships.
- Subscribe and unsubscribe views with corresponding URL patterns.
- A context processor and template updates to dynamically display subscription status in the UI.
- Email confirmation upon successful subscription, with secure credential management using `python-decouple` and a `.env` file for production-like environments.

Additionally, this commit resolves several related issues:
- Fixes a 404 error on the `/admin/` page by correctly configuring `MEDIA_URL` and `MEDIA_ROOT`.
- Corrects broken post image links by moving user-uploaded content into a `media` directory, aligning the project structure with the new settings.
- Adds the `.env` file to `.gitignore` to prevent secret credentials from being committed to version control.

author: kumsa-mergia
body:
This PR delivers a major update to the project by integrating pipeline orchestration, image enrichment, and API analytics layer. It enhances observability, automation, and accessibility of processed data.

### Key Additions
- 🧠 `notebooks/yolo_enrichment.py`: Runs object detection on scraped Telegram image folders using YOLOv8.
- 🌀 `dagster_jobs/jobs.py`: Defines a unified `telegram_etl_job` to orchestrate scraping, loading, dbt transformations, and enrichment.
- ⏰ `dagster_jobs/schedules.py`: Introduces Dagster scheduling for recurring pipeline execution.
- ⚙️ `pyproject.toml`: Declares Dagster dependencies and project settings.
- 🚀 `analytical-api/`: FastAPI server to expose enriched message and detection data via REST endpoints.
- 📘 `README.md`: Improved project documentation with detailed tech stack, setup, Dagster + FastAPI instructions, and directory overview.

author: thekingade
body:
Simplify rate limiting and streamline chatbot/document upload functionality.

The previous implementation had multiple layers of conflicting and overly restrictive rate limiting (client-side delays, server-side IP limits, AI service limits) causing frequent 'rate limit exceeded' errors and artificial delays, preventing normal HTTP request-response flow. This PR removes unnecessary complexity, increases limits to reasonable levels (60 req/min for chat, 30 req/min for uploads), and restores a direct request-response model for a smoother user experience.

author: alistairjevans
body:
Adding case-insensitive JSONExtract variants makes it much easier to search unstructured/loosely-structured data in a performant manner.

For example, we know that we want to get the "level" value from some JSON in a record, but some of the JSON data has "Level".

We can take advantage of the simdjson function `at_key_case_insensitive` (internally it does an iteration over keys with a case-insensitive strncasecmp). Compatibility function added for rapidjson.

This won't do full multi-byte-encoding-aware case-insensitive comparisons on JSON keys, but I'd add explicit UTF8 variants if those were really needed, and only if (not sure they're needed for JSON keys).

I added a CaseInsensitive variant of all JSONExtract functions that accept a sub-path.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- New Feature

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Users can now do case-insensitive JSON key lookups using `JSONExtractCaseInsensitive` (and other variants of `JSONExtract`).

author: farhin23
body:
## WHAT

This PR adds `CxPolicyDefinitionValidator `, a `JsonObjectValidator` to validate the structure of policies according to the schema defined in [cx-odrl-profile](https://github.com/catenax-eV/cx-odrl-profile). Adds support for validating ACCESS and USAGE policy types. 

## WHY

The ensure a correct structure and definition of the policies at their creation time. 

## FURTHER NOTES
* The `PolicyValidationConstants` class is intended to contain all relevant constants, including allowed constraints and left operands. Currently, it only includes the existing constraint functions and is not yet complete. Once the changes from PR(#2086) are merged, I will update this file with the new constraint left operand values. However, this PR does not depend on those changes.
* The `PolicyDefinitionEndToEndTest` class now includes additional tests to cover invalid policies with various structures.
* Some tests from certain E2E test classes (e.g., `CatalogTest`, `AbstractIatpConsumerPullTest`) have been removed, as they are no longer applicable under the newly defined policy schema. Keeping them would cause failures with the current policy validation implementation.
* In `PolicyHelperFunctions`, some method signatures have been updated, specifically to include the action type information in rules. The E2E tests using these methods have been updated accordingly.

Related to #2083

author: manuelhu
body:
* store the global position of all germanium detectors into a `detector_origins` table
    * for this, some code from vertex confinement is moved out to `RMGNavigationTools`
* in post-processing, deduplicate tables with information that is generate on all threads (such as process id to name mappings, detector coordinates)
* convert these deduplicated tables to LH5 structs (when reshaping is on, flat output keeps tables for these):
```
├── detector_origins · struct{det1,det2} 
│   ├── det1 · struct{xloc,yloc,zloc} 
│   │   ├── xloc · real 
│   │   ├── yloc · real 
│   │   └── zloc · real 
│   └── det2 · struct{xloc,yloc,zloc} 
│       ├── xloc · real 
│       ├── yloc · real 
│       └── zloc · real 
```

author: allen2c
body:
# 🚀 Cachetic v0.3.0: Type-Safe Caching Revolution! ✨

## 🎯 What's New

This is a **major rewrite** that transforms Cachetic into a modern, type-safe caching library! 

### 🔥 Breaking Changes & Improvements

🏗️ **Complete API Redesign**
- 📝 **New requirement**: All caches now use `pydantic.TypeAdapter[T]` for type safety
- 🔄 **Renamed fields**: `cache_ttl` → `default_ttl`, `cache_prefix` → `prefix`  
- 🧹 **Simplified serialization**: Everything goes through TypeAdapter (no more complex type handling)

### 📚 Documentation Overhaul

📖 **Completely rewritten README** with:
- ✨ Clean, modern examples
- 🎯 Focus on type safety and simplicity
- 📋 Better organized sections
- 🛠️ Comprehensive configuration guide

### 🧪 Test Suite Modernization

🔬 **Brand new test suite**:
- ✅ Tests for all README examples
- 🧽 Clean, isolated test setup
- 📦 Comprehensive type coverage
- 🚀 Better test organization

### 📦 Dependency Updates

⬆️ **Refreshed dependencies**:
- 🔓 Relaxed version constraints
- 📈 Updated to latest compatible versions
- 🛡️ Better security posture

## 💔 Breaking Changes

⚠️ **Migration required** for existing users:

**Before (v0.2.x):**
```python
cache = Cachetic[str](object_type=str, cache_ttl=3600, cache_prefix="app")
```

**After (v0.3.0):**
```python
cache = Cachetic[str](
    object_type=pydantic.TypeAdapter(str), 
    default_ttl=3600, 
    prefix="app"
)
```

## 🎉 Why This Matters

✨ **Better Developer Experience**:
- 🔒 Full type safety with generics
- 🎯 Simpler, more consistent API  
- 📝 Crystal clear documentation
- 🚀 Modern Python patterns

This release sets the foundation for a robust, type-safe caching experience that scales with your applications! 

---

**📋 Summary**: Major version upgrade with breaking API changes, complete documentation rewrite, modernized test suite, and focus on type safety through `pydantic.TypeAdapter`.

body: # 🎯 LTI Recruitment System Database Migration & Query Generator ## Summary Implemented a comprehensive database migration strategy for the LTI recruitment system, expanding from 4 to 13 entities with full PostgreSQL setup and advanced query generation capabilities. ## Key Changes - **Database Schema**: Migrated from basic candidate management (4 tables) to full recruitment system (13 tables) - **New Entities**: Added companies, employees, positions, applications, interviews, interview flows/steps/types - **Migration Strategy**: Preserved existing data while adding new recruitment functionality - **Docker Setup**: Configured PostgreSQL 15 container with proper credentials and networking - **Data Population**: Successfully seeded database with sample companies, candidates, and interview processes ## Technical Implementation - ✅ Prisma schema updated with relationships and constraints - ✅ Migration files generated and executed successfully - ✅ Database indexes optimized for query performance - ✅ SQL query generator prompt system created (4 complexity levels) - ✅ Example queries provided (Basic to Expert level) - ✅ Full English documentation with optimization guidelines ## Database Structure The system now supports complete recruitment workflows: candidate management → company positions → application process → interview flows → hiring decisions. ## Testing & Validation - Database connectivity verified via Docker - Complex JOIN queries tested successfully - Sample data inserted and validated - All 13 tables confirmed operational > **Note**: Prompt #3 includes screenshots demonstrating the database setup and query execution results.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Fix to allow slicing into replicated dims

I added an assert on slice_sizes to be full, but did not realize offset_dims can also be sliced dims (i.e. are in in start_index_map). We do make the check that all indexed dims are replicated, but the check on slice_size re-did this and raised an error erroneously.

We can either:
- remove the extraneous slice_sizes check
- add an extra check that non-full slices are on replicated operand

I've added the extra check version for extra caution.

> Generated on 2025-07-15 15:37:18 UTC by unknown

## Issue

The application was experiencing two critical runtime exceptions in `MainActivity.java`:

- A **NumberFormatException** occurred when attempting to parse a non-numeric date string as an integer.
- An **ArithmeticException** was triggered due to a division by zero operation.

These exceptions caused the application to crash during normal usage.

## Fix

- Updated the code to properly parse date strings using a date parser instead of `Integer.parseInt`.
- Added a check to prevent division by zero before performing arithmetic operations.

## Details

- Replaced the incorrect integer parsing of a date string with a proper date parsing approach.
- Implemented a conditional check to ensure the denominator is not zero before division.
- Changes were made in `MainActivity.java` at the affected lines (256 and 278).

## Impact

- Prevents application crashes related to invalid number parsing and division by zero.
- Improves overall application stability and user experience.
- Ensures error scenarios are handled gracefully.

## Notes

- Further input validation could be added for other user inputs to proactively prevent similar issues.
- Additional unit tests may be beneficial to cover these and related edge cases in the future.

## All Exceptions

- **NumberFormatException in simulateNumberFormatException**
  - *File:* MainActivity.java
  - *Line:* 278
  - *Cause:* Attempted to parse a date string as an integer using `Integer.parseInt`.

- **ArithmeticException in simulateArithmeticException**
  - *File:* MainActivity.java
  - *Line:* 256
  - *Cause:* Division by zero operation.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Introduced an Audio Tracks modal for managing, uploading, and generating audio tracks with infinite scroll, playback, and metadata display.
  * Added a visual audio waveform preview component for audio tracks and cards.
  * Added a prompt input control for generating audio via AI with customizable options.
  * Enabled real waveform rendering for audio tracks in the timeline.
  * Added utilities for audio file analysis and waveform extraction.

* **Enhancements**
  * Improved audio track management workflow, replacing direct file input with modal-based selection and upload.
  * Updated audio track cards to use the new audio preview component.
  * Added support for handling and caching audio files in IndexedDB.
  * Improved integration of audio tracks in project workflows and UI.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Ensured audio tracks are ordered by creation date when paginated.

* **Chores**
  * Added detailed logging for debugging track actions and auto-save triggers.

author: rugvip
body:
## Hey, I just made a Pull Request!

With catalog backend shipping 3.0 in the next release we thought it was time to include a few more changed to the default configuration:

- `disableRelationsCompatibility: true`: Relations compatibility is now disabled by default, but it can be re-enabled with the new `enableRelationsCompatibility` flag. Relations compatibility makes sure there's both `target` and `targetRef` in all relation objects, which significantly reduces overall performance of the catalog. With compatibility disabled, only the `targetRef` will be present. Only bespoke external consumers of the catalog could be affected by this change, as the `targetRef` has been in use for many years at this point.
- `orphanStrategy: 'delete'`: This switches the default orphan strategy to eagerly delete entities that are no longer referenced within the catalog.
- `orphanProviderStrategy: 'delete'`: This switches the default provider installation strategy to remove and entities that have been omitted by providers that are no longer present.
- `stitichingStrategy: { mode: 'deferred' }`: Switches the stitching strategy to happen out-of-band of the main processing loop, instead being run in a background task. This makes stitching a lot more performant in large catalogs.

These are all flags that have been around for a while and are often cited as fixes to common catalog problems. We feel it's worth switching over all of these defaults to provide a better out-of-the-box experience for the catalog. These new defaults should behave well with existing catalogs as well, but there may be some edge cases that we haven't thought of, and will be highlighting this change in the release notes.

These are in addition to the `catalog.useUrlReadersSearch` switch in https://github.com/backstage/backstage/pull/29788
